# The Next Revolution: AI, Advertising, and the Collapse of Old Media | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 30

First listed: 2025-10-20 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: The Next Revolution: AI, Advertising, and the Collapse of Old Media | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H5tBn7mV6Bc) - 2025-10-20
- [Substack: The Next Revolution: AI, Advertising, and the Collapse of Old Media](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-next-revolution-ai-advertising-5d2) - 2025-10-20

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Craig Moffett and Michael Nathanson assess Apple, cable, wireless, advertising and streaming. The guests correctly anticipate a Google-based Siri partnership and the Paramount-Warner combination, while their cable equilibrium thesis remained unproven through the cutoff. Eisman discloses modest de-risking and repeats invalid GDP-minus-total-capex arithmetic. The closing discussion carefully distinguishes AI labor savings from the fraction suppliers can capture as profits.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

### 039. Total AI capex consumes nearly all the dollar amount of forecast GDP growth, implying the rest of the economy is not growing.

**Wrong** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 51:12-51:47](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H5tBn7mV6Bc&t=3072s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Repeated material accounting error, not evidence of ex-AI stagnation.

Conditional reasoning: A $400b investment level contributes no direct incremental growth if the previous year also had $400b. Subtracting that level from GDP growth therefore creates a false residual even before adjusting inflation, imports and foreign spending.

Assessment test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.

Further verification: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

- [The expenditures approach to measuring GDP](https://www.bea.gov/index.php/news/blog/2025-06-03/expenditures-approach-measuring-gdp) (2025-06-03): GDP measures domestic production and subtracts imports embedded in expenditures; worldwide capex is not a domestic growth contribution.

## Framework and tools

- Separate operating excellence from valuation.
- Demand a catalyst and observable operating improvement for a cheap stock.
- Check density, cost per passing and cost per connected customer before extrapolating infrastructure coverage.
- Distinguish final customer demand from intercompany value-chain revenue.
- Compare willingness to pay with competitive realized price.
- Separate a successful transaction forecast from an alleged political motive.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Apple search-payment operating-profit exposure
- Cable subscriber losses, mobile growth and conditional equilibrium
- Fiber cost per connected home versus cable acquisition value
- T-Mobile valuation and demographic subscriber bridge
- Ad-share concentration and linear-TV household reach
- Final AI revenue versus capex and labor savings

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman with Craig Moffett (telecom, cable and Apple) and Michael Nathanson (advertising and media). Speaker attribution is medium confidence for guest handoffs in unlabelled captions.
- Opening montage repeats later material.
- All 1630 caption lines were read.
- Publication October 20 postdates the Verizon CEO announcement referred to as today; recording date is earlier and not precisely established here.
- Attribution uses the guests' coverage specialties and conversational handoffs; brief overlapping assent is not assigned independent forecasts.
- The claim of 100% Chinese manufacturing is preserved as a supporting factual error, not the main investment failure.
- The two guests admit their expected Google-payment catalyst did not occur.
